vikram: heads up — seeing a perf regression on TP all-reduce paths for 8-GPU runs. tail latency up ~18% and throughput drops at certain message sizes.

sam: hmm, which message sizes are we hitting? KV cache churn or model grad reductions?

vikram: mostly reduction ops coming from KV cache flushes + tensor-parallel gradient accumulation. spike around 48–80KB per rank. looks like comm becomes ring-dominated and we lose overlap.

kate: can you paste the nvprof/nvtx trace snippet? or profiler flame?

vikram: pasted below — nvtx shows long gaps where compute waits on NCCL rcv.
```
[ 0.123s ] compute kernel (6ms)
[ 0.129s ] NCCL allreduce start (12ms)
[ 0.141s ] idle (4ms)
[ 0.145s ] compute kernel (5ms)
[ 0.150s ] NCCL allreduce start (11ms)
```
Notice periodic 11–13ms allreduce steps aligned with 64KB-ish payloads.

tasha: that pattern smells like ring semantics for mid-sized messages. tree algo would shave hops for some shapes. do we have NCCL_ALGO forced anywhere in runtime? iirc we set heuristic to allow nccl to pick.

sam: runtime currently doesn't override NCCL_ALGO; we do choose chunk sizes for stream overlap but kernel selection might be picking slower kernels for these msg sizes.

vikram: confirmed: when we force NCCL_ALGO=Tree on a local repro the allreduce latency drops ~30% for those msg sizes but larger msgs regress a little.

kate: interesting. Can you share the repro command so eng-runtime folks can run quickly?

vikram: sure — minimal repro below
```
NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_ALGO=Tree ./bin/tp_microbench --gpus 8 --msg-size 65536 --iters 200
# baseline: NCCL_ALGO=Ring
```
Also instrumented with `NVPROF_USER=1` and runtime nvtx spans.

tasha: could be two contributors: 1) kernel selection: small-mid kernels use different compute kernels that shorten compute so less overlap; 2) batching heuristics: we flush KV cache updates as separate allreduces instead of coalescing. both increase number of mid-sized allreduces.

sam: agreed. quick triage plan:
- reproduce across instance types (A100 vs H100) to check hardware kernel curve
- run microbench with per-size sweep 4KB→512KB to find crossover
- toggle NCCL_ALGO tree/ring and log
- add temporary runtime flag to coalesce KV flushes by combining keys into larger tensor reductions

kate: I ran a small sweep on devbox (A100 40GB) — numbers (median allreduce ms):
- 16KB: ring 4.2ms / tree 3.9ms
- 64KB: ring 12.1ms / tree 8.3ms
- 256KB: ring 28.5ms / tree 34.2ms
So crossing point ~100KB.

vikram: exactly what i saw. For our workload distribution (lots of 48–80KB) tree is clearly better.

tasha: short-term mitigation options:
- set NCCL_ALGO=Tree in runtime for TP jobs where median msgsize < 100KB
- adjust batching window to allow coalesce of KV flush into ~128KB chunks (increase latency slightly but reduce allreduce ops)
- implement hybrid -> pick per-op algorithm based on msgsize histogram

sam: hybrid sounds ideal but needs careful testing. Also verify kernel selection: different GEMM/attention kernels might have different compute/comm balance.

vikram: i'll prototype a runtime knob that (a) records per-route msgsize histogram into console metrics, (b) exposes canary flag to force NCCL_ALGO=Tree for a given model route. We can run against the canary pool.

kate: +1. also add an A/B with batching-window=8ms vs 2ms to quantify impact on tail latency vs throughput. I expect coalescing to reduce number of calls ~3x and reduce tail.

tasha: note: KV cache eviction pattern currently causes bursts at coherent steps — if we can smooth eviction by jittering timestamps we'll reduce simultaneous allreduce fan-in.

sam: can someone post the small patch that coalesces KV flushes so we can bench? even a runtime flag that merges adjacent KV updates into a single tensor reduce is fine.

vikram: pushed a draft branch: github.com/redwood-inference/rt/tree/bugfix/allreduce-coalesce (WIP). main change in runtime/kv/coalesce.cpp — simple windowed aggregator.

ci-bot: CI queued for branch allreduce-coalesce, job #4821 — will run perf microbench.

kate: ran the branch locally: with coalesce-window=8ms on A100 devbox I got end-to-end throughput +9% and 95p latency -22% for our test route. nice.

tasha: good. caveats: need to ensure correctness for ordering and no memory blow-up when coalescing many keys. add guard for max-coalesce-bytes.

vikram: noted. plan:
1) run full microbench sweep across gpus (A100/H100) with Tree vs Ring vs hybrid and coalesce on/off (target: today EOD)
2) if stable, flip canary for small-model-shard routes for limited traffic (nightly low-traffic window)
3) collect console histograms and compare cost/latency tradeoffs

sam: assign owners: vikram proto + canary rollout, kate bench matrix, tasha safety checks and max-bytes guard. I'll help interpret kernel profiles.

vikram: thanks. will post results in this thread once sweep completes. :eyes:

ci-bot: perf job #4821 completed — microbench results uploaded to http://ci.internal/perf/4821

vikram: saw the CI results — consistent with local: tree + coalesce wins for our workload. scheduling a short sync tomorrow 10:30 to decide canary parameters.

kate: ack. I'll bring the raw csv and plots.

sam: thanks all. small follow-ups: add unit test for coalesce max-bytes and a trace test for correct NVTX spans.

vikram: adding those tests now. will tag you when ready @sam @kate @tasha.
